new_page.title: Vancouver Townhomes for Sale | Kitsilano to Cambie
new_page.description: Search Vancouver townhomes for sale. Compare Kitsilano, Fairview, Cambie and Collingwood sold prices, days to sell and strata fees by complex.

faq.q: How much is a townhome in Vancouver?
faq.a: Over the year to October 22, 2026 the median was $1,405,000 in Kitsilano, $1,080,000 in Fairview, $1,502,500 in Cambie and $981,500 in Collingwood. The townhouse benchmark was $1,285,000 in Vancouver West and $1,055,800 in Vancouver East.

faq.q: Which Vancouver neighbourhood sells the most townhomes?
faq.a: Kitsilano (70 sales), Fairview (66), Mount Pleasant East (40) and Cambie (36).

faq.q: How fast do Vancouver townhomes sell?
faq.a: Quickly on the West Side: 12 days in Kitsilano and 13 in Fairview. Champlain Heights is slower at 44.

faq.q: What are strata fees for Vancouver townhomes?
faq.a: Median fees ran from $362 in Collingwood to $864 in University.
Over one year the benchmark moved -5.7% in Vancouver West and 0.4% in Vancouver East.

faq.q: Are there new townhomes in Vancouver?
faq.a: Yes. Cambie and Collingwood medians were built in 2024 and 2023. For projects not yet built, see the presale condos and townhomes page.

blocks.text: This search lists townhomes for sale in the city of Vancouver: strata homes with their own front door, from Kitsilano and Fairview to Cambie and the East Side complexes. Houses and condos are separate searches.

597 Vancouver townhomes closed in the year to October 22, 2026: 367 in Vancouver West and 230 in Vancouver East, across 31 neighbourhoods. Kitsilano led with 70 at $1,405,000, Fairview had 66 at $1,080,000. There is no one city median in the sold records, so each neighbourhood is shown on its own.

These sell fast. Kitsilano townhomes took 12 days at a median and Fairview 13, both under two weeks. Cambie is the newest and dearest of the larger groups: 36 sales at $1,502,500, median built 2024, in 26 days. University is the exception on fees at $864 a month.

blocks.text: Prices on the East Side start near $929,000 in Champlain Heights, where the median complex was built in 1981 and homes took 44 days. Collingwood sold at $981,500 (26 sales, built 2023), Grandview Woodland at $1,085,000 and Mount Pleasant East at $1,304,500 in 10 days.

blocks.text: Most Vancouver townhomes are strata lots, so the strata’s minutes and depreciation report matter as much as the unit. The BC townhome buying rules page lists the documents. The Tenant Relocation and Protection Policy applies citywide to rented buildings that are redeveloped, and the Empty Homes Tax is 3% of assessed value for a home that is not occupied or rented.

items.t: Check the age of the complex. Champlain Heights townhomes were built around 1981 and Cambie around 2024.
Compare fees inside the same neighbourhood. The median ran from $362 a month in Collingwood to $864 in University.
Ask what parking comes with the unit.
For a new complex, ask for the warranty details and the completion date.
